content: Food insecurity is characterized by inconsistent or unreliable access to sufficient and nutritious food. Among adults living with diabetes, approximately 16% experience food insecurity. It is essential to implement screening for food insecurity at all levels of healthcare to identify individuals who may be at risk. Once identified, these individuals should be referred to appropriate support services or resources. Screening typically involves asking specific questions, such as whether a household runs out of food before they are able to obtain more, to evaluate the level of risk.
